subject: EU data sovereignty MAP kickoff: roles, evaluation plan, timeline
thread:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@eurobank.com>, Thomas Berg <t.berg@data-governance.consulting>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU data sovereignty MAP kickoff: roles, evaluation plan, timeline

Hi Anna / Thomas —

Thanks for agreeing to kick off the mutual action plan for EuroBank's EU data residency & cross-border review. I want to put a clean starting point on the calendar and align on owners, a lightweight evaluation plan, and closing milestones so we can hit the requested production window.

Attached: MAP_DRAFT_v1.xlsx (draft milestones & owners), evaluation_criteria.md (what Redwood will evaluate: data flows, control points, latency/region tests).

Quick summary / asks:
- Goal: Complete MAP + evaluation and sign-off by 2026-12-20 so engineering work can start in Q1 provisioning EU-dedicated capacity.
- Proposed owners: EuroBank security (Anna) owns acceptance criteria for data locality & legal sign-off; EuroBank infra (Thomas) owns network/VPC connectivity; Redwood will own deployment plan, canary/testing, and providing SOC 2 + data flow diagrams.
- Key milestones in the attached sheet: discovery (this week), evidentiary exchange (by 11/20), evaluation window (11/22–12/10), final decision & contract addendum (by 12/20).

Please: confirm the list of internal EuroBank stakeholders (security/infra/legal), and flag any missing acceptance criteria in evaluation_criteria.md. If all good, suggest 30 minutes for an internal+external sync — I can host Wed 11/11 10:00–10:30 CET or Thu 11/12 14:00–14:30 CET.

Attaching a quick stub of expected deliverables.

Thanks — looking forward to collaborating.

—
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0168

Attachments: MAP_DRAFT_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), evaluation_criteria.md (text)

Thanks Diego — and hi Thomas.

EuroBank will own final acceptance on data residency and legal vetting. My suggested roster:
- Anna Müller (security lead, data residency) — primary sign-off
- Markus Klein (legal, privacy) — contract & transfer language
- Sofia Kauppi (external counsel) — regulatory review (cc'd Thomas for coordination)
- Infrastructure: Thomas (cc'd) or his deputy for VPC/peering details

Two asks from our side before the sync:
1) Can you share a data flow diagram (PII / non-PII separation) and a short note on cross-border fallbacks (where tokens/cache might be served from during failovers)?
2) We need SOC 2 + pen test summary to share with our procurement team; a redacted report link or location is fine.

We can do Wed 11/11 10:00 CET. If you prefer, Thu 11/12 14:00 also works.

Also attaching a small CSV with security contacts for scheduling — euobank_security_contacts.csv.

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU data sovereignty MAP kickoff: roles, evaluation plan, timeline

Anna — thanks for the quick response and roster. I’ll be the account lead on the deal and will coordinate procurement redlines and timing with Markus (legal). Couple of clarifications from Redwood:

- Data flow diagram: Diego will send a redacted architecture diagram this afternoon. It will show separation of PII/Non-PII, keys staying in customer KMS, and how KV cache prefixing avoids cross-customer leakage.
- Cross-border fallback: Redwood's default routing policy will prefer EU-serving shards; if EU capacity is unavailable we can auto-failover to a designated secondary (we propose Ireland as standby) — we’ll include clear SLAs and an automatic notification policy in the MAP.
- Evidence pack: SOC 2 certificate + 1-page pen test summary are available; I’ll drop links in HubSpot and send a doc for procurement review.

Proposed immediate milestones (I updated the attached spreadsheet):
1) Discovery meeting (Wed 11/11 10:00 CET) — confirm owners and acceptance criteria
2) Evidence exchange (by 11/19) — SOC2, pen test summary, data flow diagram
3) Evaluation window (11/22–12/06) — Redwood to run a staged canary in EU region with pre-agreed workload; EuroBank to run acceptance tests
4) Contract addendum & sign-off (by 12/20)

Next steps: Diego — please share the redacted diagram and a short one-pager describing the canary test plan. I’ll create a HubSpot task for procurement review and include a DocuSign link for the amendment once commercial terms are agreed.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: EU data sovereignty MAP kickoff: roles, evaluation plan, timeline — next steps

Thanks everyone — great sync this morning. Short notes and confirmed actions:

- Diego: share redacted data flow diagram and one-page canary plan (sent to Anna/Markus).
- Marissa: create HubSpot evidence task and link SOC2/pen test; draft contract addendum and share DocuSign link.
- Anna / EuroBank: confirm Markus and legal review completion target 12/08.
- Thomas: confirm VPC peering details and expected time for test provisioning (target 11/22).

We will treat the evaluation window as 11/22–12/06 with an internal checkpoint on 11/29 to review test results. If the acceptance tests pass, legal can finalize the addendum by 12/20.

Closing note: Redwood can enable an EU-dedicated canary cluster with the following guarded defaults — strict prefix isolation, customer KMS for keys, and failover policies that route to EU-first shards. We will record all test runs and provide token-level latency/cost breakdowns for your acceptance criteria.

I’ll follow up with the attachments and a calendar invite for the evidence-exchange checklist.
